method: fresh subagent per case with only SKILL.md and the prompt; separate grader

checks.check: Assigns unique IDs to all three comments (e.g. R1.1, R1.2, R2.1).
checks.reason: Labels the comments 'Comment R1.1', 'Comment R1.2' and 'Comment R2.1'.

checks.check: Classifies each comment as Accept, Partial, or Pushback, or asks the author to confirm the classification.
checks.reason: States 'I've drafted all three comments as accepted (A)', and the note after the letter asks the author to confirm or change R2.1 to Partial/Pushback.

checks.check: The R1.1 response acknowledges the omission and says a description of how matched controls were selected has been added, without stating any matching variables, tolerances, method names or table numbers the user did not supply (placeholders are fine).
checks.reason: R1.1 says it 'should have been described explicitly' and 'We have added a description of the matching procedure to [location]'. Method, criteria, thresholds/calipers and any table/supplement are all bracketed ('[matching method...]', '[matching criteria/covariates used]'). No named method, variable, tolerance or table number.

checks.check: The R1.2 response accepts the change without inventing a specific new figure size or font size.
checks.reason: R1.2 says 'We have revised Figure 3 by [what you changed, e.g. new figure size, larger axis label font...]'. No size or font value is given.

checks.check: The R2.1 response engages specifically with the causation point, without inventing section, paragraph or sentence locations the user did not supply.
checks.reason: R2.1 engages with the point ('supports an association ... not a definitive causal effect'). Locations are '[location(s), e.g. the Discussion and Conclusion sections...]', and the reviewer named those sections, so nothing is invented.

checks.check: Every specific not given by the user appears as a bracketed placeholder, and the output lists the placeholders for the author to fill in.
checks.reason: Every unknown (method, criteria, thresholds, figure change, locations, causal rewording, policy framing) is bracketed and listed in the 12-item 'Placeholders to fill in'. Numbers used (>20%, 1.8–3.2°C) are from the prompt. Borderline but acceptable: the unbracketed 'Our empirical findings are unchanged' is a claim the author didn't make, though it is implied by a wording-only change.

checks.check: Includes an opening paragraph thanking the reviewers.
checks.reason: Opens with 'We thank the editor and both reviewers for their careful reading...'.

checks.check: Includes a closing summary of major changes.
checks.reason: Has a 'Summary of major changes' section with bullets, locations bracketed.

checks.check: Output is paste-ready in standard academic response letter format, apart from the marked placeholders.
checks.reason: The letter sits between '---' separators in the 'Dear Editor and Reviewers' / Comment / Response / Summary format, so it can be pasted once the marked placeholders are filled.

checks.check: Acknowledges the limitation the reviewer identified (parental diary underestimation) substantively.
checks.reason: R1.1 says 'relying only on parental diary reports is an important limitation' and discusses the direction of bias, including the caveat that under-reporting might differ by SES or parental education.

checks.check: Presents both options the reviewer offered and, since the user hasn't said which path they are taking, asks them rather than choosing for them.
checks.reason: Splits (a) and (b) into R1.2 and R1.3 with an 'Option if...' block for each. It does not choose: 'Please tell me which route you're taking', and placeholder 1 asks 'which of (a) or (b) you are answering'.

checks.check: Does not dismiss or minimise the measurement concern.
checks.reason: Takes the concern seriously throughout, e.g. 'we agree that the effect sizes should be interpreted with the measurement limitation in mind'. Even the Pushback option offers an alternative step.

checks.check: Suggests specific manuscript changes (e.g. revised limitation section language, or framing as pilot).
checks.reason: Proposes concrete edits, e.g. revise '[Abstract, Discussion] to state that ... the reported effect sizes may be underestimates', and expand the limitations discussion of parent-reported screen time.

checks.check: Does not invent device-log data that was not provided.
checks.reason: All device-log details are placeholders ('subsample of [n] children', '[device/app used]', '[correlation / mean difference]'). No device data is invented.

checks.check: Maintains a professional, collegial tone throughout.
checks.reason: Collegial throughout ('We appreciate the reviewer's suggestion', 'We thank the reviewer for this alternative').

checks.check: Does not assert facts about the study's design, power or data that the user didn't supply (bracketed placeholders are fine).
checks.reason: In the R1.3 Partial option, the unbracketed sentence 'A prospective cohort of 847 children ... was designed and powered as a full study' asserts that the study was powered, which the user never said. The following '[add your power analysis or design rationale if you have one]' bracket asks for supporting detail but does not make the claim itself conditional.

checks.check: Asks for the paper title and abstract or summary before drafting responses.
checks.reason: Asks for '1. The paper's title' and '2. A brief summary: the abstract, or 3-5 sentences'.

checks.check: Does not draft responses without knowing what the paper is about.
checks.reason: Only restates and labels the two comments; says 'Before I draft anything, I need some context'.

checks.check: Does not invent paper details.
checks.reason: Makes no claims about the paper. Possible actions (power analysis, exploratory reframing) are put as questions to the author.

checks.check: Specifies exactly what information it needs to proceed.
checks.reason: Lists numbered items: title and summary (required), then decisions and changes and the journal name (optional).

checks.check: Identifies that the reviewer comment is internally contradictory (failed statistical test vs. visual parallel trends).
checks.reason: Under '1. The comment contradicts itself.' it sets Claim A (p=0.049 is 'a failed parallel trends test') against Claim B ('Figure 2 clearly shows parallel trends visually').

checks.check: Flags the contradiction to the author rather than drafting a response that ignores it.
checks.reason: Flags it before drafting: 'I'd like to check two things with you before I draft the response, because this comment pulls in two directions'.

checks.check: Asks the author how they want to handle the tension before drafting.
checks.reason: Asks 'How do you want to handle this?' and offers options (a) to (d) with 'you choose; I won't pick one for you'.

checks.check: Does not invent a resolution or additional statistical analysis.
checks.reason: Proposes no result or analysis as done. Analyses appear only as questions ('what you ran (for example, a different event window...)'). One caveat: option (a) assumes 'one significant pre-period coefficient out of several', a pre-period count the prompt doesn't give, although the output then asks 'how many pre-periods there are'.

checks.check: Does not draft a response that accepts or rejects the comment wholesale without addressing the contradiction.
checks.reason: Drafts no response at all and defers until the author has decided how to handle the tension.

checks.check: Asks for the reviewer comments before proceeding.
checks.reason: 'Before I can draft anything, I need the reviewer comments themselves', and item 1 lists them as required.

checks.check: Does not draft a generic response letter without the actual comments.
checks.reason: No letter drafted; 'I won't start without them'.

checks.check: Does not invent plausible reviewer comments.
checks.reason: No reviewer comments invented. Only generic placeholder examples ('[section]', '[new sample size]').

checks.check: Also asks for or confirms paper context if not provided.
checks.reason: Item 2 requires 'Paper context (required). The title plus the abstract, or a 3 to 5 sentence summary'.

checks.check: Declines to write an angry or dismissive response.
checks.reason: 'I've kept the letter respectful rather than telling the reviewer they're wrong', and explains why.

checks.check: Acknowledges the author's disagreement with the reviewer and validates the substance of the pushback.
checks.reason: 'You can disagree firmly here ... you are not switching to a narrative synthesis, and the letter says why'. The letter builds on the author's two points (heterogeneity is normal; random effects are designed for it).

checks.check: Drafts a professional pushback response that cites the methodological justification (random-effects models handle heterogeneity) without being dismissive of the reviewer.
checks.reason: The 'Second' paragraph explains that a random-effects model 'does not assume that all studies share one true effect' and accounts for between-study variance. It opens 'We thank the reviewer' and concedes 'The I² of 78% is substantial'.

checks.check: Maintains a collegial tone in the drafted response.
checks.reason: Measured wording throughout: 'we respectfully disagree', 'we agree that it must be considered'.

checks.check: Does not simply capitulate to the reviewer's demand if the author has a valid methodological defence.
checks.reason: Keeps the meta-analysis: 'we have kept the quantitative synthesis for the following reasons'. The summary option is 'retained the random-effects meta-analysis'.

checks.check: R1.1 is classified Accept and its response states the exclusion count (27) and criterion (fewer than 5 valid nights) in Section 2.2, exactly as given.
checks.reason: R1.1 response: 'We now report in Section 2.2 that 27 participants were excluded because they had fewer than 5 valid nights of actigraphy data', exactly as given. The letter format has no explicit 'Accept' label, but the response is a full acceptance with the change made, which is the skill's definition of Accept.

checks.check: R1.2 is classified Partial and its response says caffeine was not collected and that it was added as a limitation in Section 4.3, paragraph 2.
checks.reason: R1.2 response: 'we did not collect caffeine intake data' and 'added the absence of caffeine data as a limitation in Section 4.3, paragraph 2'. It accepts the concern and makes a narrower change, which is Partial. There is no explicit label, as with R1.1.

checks.check: Adds no numbers, analyses, sections or citations beyond what the user supplied.
checks.reason: The only numbers and sections are 27, 5 valid nights, Section 2.2 and Section 4.3 paragraph 2. 'Models, which control for prior GPA' comes from the summary. No new analyses or citations.

checks.check: Contains no bracketed placeholders, because the user supplied every needed detail.
checks.reason: There are no square-bracket placeholders anywhere in the output.

checks.check: Includes an opening paragraph and a closing summary of major changes.
checks.reason: Opening paragraph ('Thank you for the opportunity to revise our manuscript...') and a 'Summary of major changes' with two bullets.

notes: Re-run after eval c1 in the first run passed an output that invented methods details. One FAIL kept as graded: in c2 the skill asserted the study was powered as a full study, which the user never said. Close calls graded PASS are listed in the grader report: c1 states findings are unchanged; c7 has no explicit A/B/C labels; c4 assumes a count of pre-periods in a suggested argument.
